See how many peoples the Church contains, which dwells upon the rivers of the prophets, and has round about her teachers out of whose belly flow rivers; which are enriched by the spiritual sense of the law, which without faith in Christ is bitter; which has for walls the multitude of peoples, or of the Scriptures, which those once black and dark and dry make firm. But even she, if she does not attend to herself and keep her heart, will be led captive, and will lament her sons, who will be dashed in pieces before they come to the middle of the road; and the enemies, the devils, will hasten to divide among themselves by lot whatever is most splendid in her; and the great men, that is, those set over her, will be bound in the fetters of sins. How much more, then, will you unbelievers, who cling to the world, feel punishments and be despised? And you will seek help from the enemy, that the vices and demons may cease to pursue you; but all your strong holds, worldly sweetness, power, teachings, will be devoured by the devil, the eater, at the first shaking of the tree.
**“are its walls”** — The city which is now called Alexandria, after Alexander the Great, was before called No, the capital of Egypt; and this prophet called it by its old name, No, but the translator called it Alexandria, which was its name in his time.
3.9:
**“Ethiopia and Egypt were the strength thereof”** — that Ethiopia and Egypt and Africa are the defence of Alexandria the very position of the provinces and of the city shows; these peoples were allied
**“and there is no end”** — to her strength, or her wealth
**“Africa and the Libyans were thy helpers”** — O Alexandria
3.10:
**“Yet she also was removed and carried into captivity”** — The city I describe will be taken by the Babylonian king, and the same will lay waste both you and her.
**“young children”** — who could not walk
**“her”** — Alexandria's
**“were dashed in pieces”** — by the enemy
**“at the top”** — before their fathers' faces
**“of every street”** — at the crossroads
**“and they cast lots upon her nobles”** — the nobles will be divided by the victors' lot
**“and all her great men were bound in fetters”** — none of the princes will escape
3.11: **“Therefore thou also shalt be made drunk”** — Since Alexandria is to suffer these things, you too, O Ninive, once rich and beautiful, drinking of the same cup, will be made drunk, and, lying stupefied, will be despised by all; and, coming into such need, you will ask help from the Babylonians, or against the Babylonians from your enemies.
3.12: **“All thy strong holds”** — which you think impregnable, and your strong men, are compared to the first figs, which, moved by a light touch, fall without effort into the mouth of the eater, lest, if they fell on the ground, they should give labour to the one gathering them.
3.13:
**“Behold”** — O Ninive, no wonder if you are devoured so, since a people so unmanned cannot resist the enemy
**“thy people”** — as
**“are women”** — as weak as
**“in the midst of thee”** — therefore
**“the gates of thy land shall be set wide open to thy enemies”** — the city will be laid open to the enemy
**“the fire shall devour thy bars”** — with which the gates were shut
**“Behold thy people”**
• Morally. Ninive, which is called beautiful, signifies the soul, by nature fair, which, clinging to pleasures, is unmanned, and opens the gates of the senses to vices and demons. For if anyone is a lover of pleasures more than of God, he has opened the gates of his land to the enemy; and the bars of this Babylon will be consumed by fire, that is, the natural good of the soul, by which it could shut against the enemy the road of the bodily senses. To her it is said that she should draw to herself the water of the divine word as a wall, and hold fast the natural good of the soul as it were, so that the enemy may not break through to the inner parts. There follows: Go into the clay: that is, you who have entangled yourself in various evils, bear patiently the wrongs of temptation; otherwise you will perish and lose all your natural good. Against these things, multiply yourself in as great a number of virtues as is the number of the bruchus.
• Allegorically. O Ninive, your people, that is, all worldly men, are so enervated by vices that they have nothing manly. Hence the enemies, namely the demons, or the vices, have entered through the open bodily senses; and they also, like fire, devour the natural power of knowing God, which ought to have barred the gates of the senses. Against these evils draw water for yourself: sprinkle yourself with the word and with reason; exercise yourself in the knowledge of God through the virtues planted in you; and do penance for having fallen. This is what he says: Go into the clay: bear the wrong patiently, and the necessity of the body in which you are wrapped; and, working it, that is, bringing into servitude the brick, that is, the body, tread it and hold it, so that it does not rule over you; because, if you remain there, that is, in the body, the living flame either of the vices here, or of hell hereafter, will consume you; and you will perish by the sword, that is, by the violent assault of the devil. And, after the likeness of locusts, whatever seemed green in you, and the good of nature springing up of itself, is consumed by the bruchus eating it. But so that this may not happen, multiply yourself in virtues as innumerable as the bruchus. All these punishments you have suffered because you have multiplied your merchandises above the stars of heaven: because you gathered for yourself perishing riches by right and wrong; or you thought various teachings brighter than the stars; and, walking by the broad way, running to and fro in the softness of your opinion, you raised yourself to the heights; and your guards, that is, those set over you, were like locusts, raising themselves to the flight of heresy, but quickly falling down; and your little ones, that is, those born of the locusts, were like the attelebus, lifting themselves a little from the ground, so that at last they may grow into a locust. These, lacking the warmth of the true sun, sit on thorny seats, that is, the rough opinions of the philosophers. But when the sunrise comes, that is, the judgement of true knowledge, they leave their thorns and pass into pure and free flight.
3.14:
**“Draw thee water for the siege”** — so that those besieged may not lack drink
**“build up thy bulwarks”** — walls, towers
**“go into the clay, and tread, work it and make brick”** — make bricks, so that you may build up the breaches in the walls
3.15:
**“There shall the fire devour thee: thou shalt perish by the sword, it shall devour thee like the bruchus: assemble together like”** — as
**“the bruchus, make thyself many like the locust”** — and when you have done all these things, as the ground by the bruchus, so you will be devoured by the sword of a raging army
**“assemble together”** — And when you have been multiplied like the bruchus, and gathered into one like the locust, and have gathered riches like the stars of heaven: as the locust and the bruchus and the attelebus, which is the young of the locust, fly away when the sun grows warm and are not found, so you will be scattered and flee.
3.16:
**“Thou hast multiplied thy merchandises above the stars of heaven”**
• and
• as
**“the bruchus hath spread himself and flown away”** — its wings grown for flying
3.17:
**“Thy guards are like the locusts: and thy little ones like the locusts of locusts which swarm on the hedges in the day of cold: the sun arose, and they flew away, and their place was not known where they were”**
• because they cannot fly away
• but when
• warmed
• to other regions
• they do not remember the hedge on which they sat in the time of cold
• It is the nature of locusts to grow numb in the cold and to fly about in the heat.
• Further, the attelebus, with small wings, creeping rather than flying, consumes everything down to the dust wherever it springs up, because it cannot go away until its wings grow.
3.18:
**“have slumbered”**
• with the numbness of sloth
• Because your people are like women, and the gates are open to the enemy, and the whole multitude sitting on the wall is like locusts, which, as if at the dawning of the sun, at the coming of Nabuchodonosor, flee from the ramparts and do not return to their place; all of which God, angry, brought on you for laying waste his people; therefore your city is destroyed.
• Since up to here the ruin of the world has been spoken of, at the end the wound of the devil himself is spoken of, who was the prince of the world and boasted that he ruled in it; to whom this apostrophe is made: O Lucifer, you are crushed; destroyed is Ninive, your beautiful and powerful city, in which you set yourself even against the Son of God. The shepherds who fed the people, not for salvation but so that you might devour them, have failed. The crowd of the people that worshipped you, leaving you and your city, has fled to the hiding places of the mountains, that is, of the apostles, and there is none of your leaders to call back to himself the crowd that was once yours. Your wound has resounded through the whole world. All insult you who before were deceived by your tripping. For there is no one, or scarcely anyone, whom you have not at some time deceived. He in whom the malice of the devil does not stay, but passes, can insult him, and clap over him with good works as with outstretched hands.
**“Thy shepherds … O king of Assyria”** — the kings from other nations who served you
**“thy princes shall be buried: thy people are hid in the mountains, and there is none to gather them together”** — and, the princes who could have resisted being killed, the people was scattered in the wars, and none of the leaders could gather them and lead them back into battle.
3.19:
**“Thy destruction is not hidden, thy wound is grievous”** — because it cannot be cured by the physician's hand
**“all that have heard the fame of thee, have clapped their hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?”** — no one will give tears for your wound, because there is no one over whom your malice had not passed, which does not abide but passes.
**“all that have heard the fame”** — The nations oppressed by you, hearing of the death of the proud Assyrian and the destruction of the mighty city, will press their hands together in wonder at the unhoped-for news, or, insulting you for joy, will clap their hands.

1.text: The word of the Lord, that came to Osee the son of Beeri, in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias kings of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel.

2.text: The beginning of the Lord’s speaking by Osee: and the Lord said to Osee: Go, take thee a wife of fornications, and have of her children of fornications: for the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord.

3.text: So he went, and took Gomer the daughter of Debelaim: and she conceived and bore him a son.

4.text: And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezrahel: for yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezrahel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.

5.text: And in that day I will break in pieces the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezrahel.

6.text: And she conceived again, and bore a daughter, and he said to him: Call her name, Without mercy: for I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them.

7.text: And I will have mercy on the house of Juda, and I will save them by the Lord their God: and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, nor by horses, nor by horsemen.

8.text: And she weaned her that was called Without mercy. And she conceived, and bore a son.

9.text: And he said: Call his name, Not my people: for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.

10.text: And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, that is without measure, and shall not be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God.

11.text: And the children of Juda, and the children of Israel shall be gathered together: and they shall appoint themselves one head, and shall come up out of the land: for great is the day of Jezrahel.

1.text: Say ye to your brethren: You are my people, and to your sister: Thou hast obtained mercy.

2.text: Judge your mother, judge her: because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts.

3.text: Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born: and I will make her as a wilderness, and will set her as a land that none can pass through, and will kill her with drought.

4.text: And I will not have mercy on her children: for they are the children of fornications.

5.text: For their mother hath committed fornication, she that conceived them is covered with shame: for she said: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, my oil, and my drink.

6.text: Wherefore behold I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths.

7.text: And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, and shall not find, and she shall say: I will go, and return to my first husband, because it was better with me then, than now.

8.text: And she did not know that I gave her corn and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver, and gold, which they have used in the service of Baal.

9.text: Therefore will I return, and take away my corn in its season, and my wine in its season, and I will set at liberty my wool, and my flax, which covered her disgrace.

10.text: And now I will lay open her folly in the eyes of her lovers: and no man shall deliver her out of my hand:

11.text: And I will cause all her mirth to cease, her solemnities, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her festival times.

12.text: And I will destroy her vines, and her fig trees, of which she said: These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me: and I will make her as a forest, and the beasts of the field shall devour her.

13.text: And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim, to whom she burnt incense, and decked herself out with her earrings, and with her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, saith the Lord.

14.text: Therefore, behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart.

15.text: And I will give her vinedressers out of the same place, and the valley of Achor for an opening of hope: and she shall sing there according to the days of her youth, and according to the days of her coming up out of the land of Egypt.

16.text: And it shall be in that day, saith the Lord, That she shall call me: My husband, and she shall call me no more Baali.

17.text: And I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and she shall no more remember their name.

18.text: And in that day I will make a covenant with them, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air, and with the creeping things of the earth: and I will destroy the bow, and the sword, and war out of the land: and I will make them sleep secure.

19.text: And I will espouse thee to me for ever: and I will espouse thee to me in justice, and judgment, and in mercy, and in commiserations.

20.text: And I will espouse thee to me in faith: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.

21.text: And it shall come to pass in that day: I will hear, saith the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.

22.text: And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil, and these shall hear Jezrahel.

23.text: And I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercy on her that was without mercy. And I will say to that which was not my people: Thou art my people: and they shall say: Thou art my God.

1.text: And the Lord said to me: Go yet again, and love a woman beloved of her friend, and an adulteress: as the Lord loveth the children of Israel, and they look to strange gods, and love the husks of the grapes.

2.text: And I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for a core of barley, and for half a core of barley.

3.text: And I said to her: Thou shalt wait for me many days: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be no man’s, and I also will wait for thee.

4.text: For the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim.

5.text: And after this the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the Lord their God, and David their king: and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness in the last days.

1.text: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel, for the Lord shall enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the land: for there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land.

2.text: Cursing, and lying, and killing, and theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood hath touched blood.

3.text: Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth in it shall languish with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air: yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be gathered together.

4.text: But yet let not any man judge: and let not a man be rebuked: for thy people are as they that contradict the priest.

5.text: And thou shalt fall today, and the prophet also shall fall with thee: in the night I have made thy mother to be silent.

6.text: My people have been silent, because they had no knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me: and thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I also will forget thy children.

7.text: According to the multitude of them so have they sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame.

8.text: They shall eat the sins of my people, and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity.

9.text: And there shall be like people like priest: and I will visit their ways upon them, and I will repay them their devices.

10.text: And they shall eat and shall not be filled: they have committed fornication, and have not ceased: because they have forsaken the Lord in not observing his law.

11.text: Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness take away the understanding.

12.text: My people have consulted their stocks, and their staff hath declared unto them: for the spirit of fornication hath deceived them, and they have committed fornication against their God.

13.text: They offered sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burnt incense upon the hills: under the oak, and the poplar, and the turpentine tree, because the shadow thereof was good: therefore shall your daughters commit fornication, and your spouses shall be adulteresses.

14.text: I will not visit upon your daughters when they shall commit fornication, and upon your spouses when they shall commit adultery: because themselves conversed with harlots, and offered sacrifice with the effeminate, and the people that doth not understand shall be beaten.

15.text: If thou play the harlot, O Israel, at least let not Juda offend: and go ye not into Galgal, and come not up into Bethaven, and do not swear: The Lord liveth.

16.text: For Israel hath gone astray like a wanton heifer: now will the Lord feed them, as a lamb in a spacious place.

17.text: Ephraim is a partaker with idols, let him alone.

18.text: Their banquet is separated, they have gone astray by fornication: they that should have protected them have loved to bring shame upon them.

19.text: The wind hath bound them up in its wings, and they shall be confounded because of their sacrifices.

1.text: Hear ye this, O priests, and hearken, O ye house of Israel, and give ear, O house of the king: for there is a judgment against you, because you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over, and a net spread upon Thabor.

2.text: And you have turned aside victims into the depth: and I am, the teacher of them all.

3.text: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now Ephraim hath committed fornication, Israel is defiled.

4.text: They will not set their thoughts to return to their God: for the spirit of fornication is in the midst of them, and they have not known the Lord.

5.text: And the pride of Israel shall answer in his face: and Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity, Juda also shall fall with them.

6.text: With their flocks, and with their herds, they shall go to seek the Lord, and shall not find him: he is withdrawn from them.

7.text: They have transgressed against the Lord, for they have begotten children that are strangers: now shall a month devour them with their portions.

8.text: Blow ye the cornet in Gabaa, the trumpet in Rama: howl ye in Bethaven, behind thy back, O Benjamin.

9.text: Ephraim shall be in desolation in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel I have shewn that which shall surely be.

10.text: The princes of Juda are become as they that take up the bound: I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.

11.text: Ephraim is under oppression, and broken in judgment: because he began to go after filthiness.

12.text: And I will be like a moth to Ephraim: and like rottenness to the house of Juda.

13.text: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Juda his band: and Ephraim went to the Assyrian, and sent to the avenging king: and he shall not be able to heal you, neither shall he be able to take off the band from you.

14.text: For I will be like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion’s whelp to the house of Juda: I, I will catch, and go: I will take away, and there is none that can rescue.

15.text: I will go and return to my place: until you are consumed, and seek my face.

1.text: In their affliction they will rise early to me: Come, and let us return to the Lord: For he hath taken us, and he will heal us: he will strike, and he will cure us.

2.text: He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on, that we may know the Lord. His going forth is prepared as the morning light, and he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth.

3.text: He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on, that we may know the Lord. His going forth is prepared as the morning light, and he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth.

4.text: What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim? what shall I do to thee, O Juda? your mercy is as a morning cloud, and as the dew that goeth away in the morning.

5.text: For this reason have I hewed them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments shall go forth as the light.

6.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts.

7.text: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant, there have they dealt treacherously against me.

8.text: Galaad is a city of workers of idols, supplanted with blood.

9.text: And like the jaws of highway robbers, they conspire with the priests who murder in the way those that pass out Sichem: for they have wrought wickedness.

10.text: I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel: the fornications of Ephraim there: Israel is defiled.

11.text: And thou also, O Juda, set thee a harvest, when I shall bring back captivity of my people.

1.text: When I would have healed Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria, for they have committed falsehood, and the thief is come in to steal, the robber is without.

2.text: And lest they may say in their hearts, that I remember all their wickedness: their own devices now have beset them about, they have been done before my face.

3.text: They have made the king glad with their wickedness: and the princes with their lies.

4.text: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker: the city rested a little from the mingling of the leaven, till the whole was leavened.

5.text: The day of our king, the princes began to be mad with wine: he stretched out his hand with scorners.

6.text: Because they have applied their heart like an oven, when he laid snares for them: he slept all the night baking them, in the morning he himself was heated as a flaming fire.

7.text: They were all heated like an oven, and have devoured their judges: all their kings have fallen: there is none amongst them that calleth unto me.

8.text: Ephraim himself is mixed among the nations: Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes, that is not turned.

9.text: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knew it not: yea, grey hairs also are spread about upon him, and he is ignorant of it.

10.text: And the pride of Israel shall be humbled before his face: and they have not returned to the Lord their God, nor have they sought him in all these.

11.text: And Ephraim is become as a dove that is decoyed, not having a heart: they called upon Egypt, they went to the Assyrians.

12.text: And when they shall go, I will spread my net upon them: I will bring them down as the fowl of the air, I will strike them as their congregation hath heard.

13.text: Woe to them, for they have departed from me: they shall be wasted because they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me.

14.text: And they have not cried to me with their heart, but they howled in their beds: they have thought upon wheat and wine, they are departed from me.

15.text: And I have chastised them, and strengthened their arms: and they have imagined evil against me.

16.text: They returned, that they might be without yoke: they became like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword, for the rage of their tongue. This is their derision in the land of Egypt.

1.text: Let there be a trumpet in thy throat like an eagle upon the house of the Lord: because they have transgressed my covenant, and have violated my law.

2.text: They shall call upon me: O my God, we, Israel, know thee.

3.text: Israel hath cast off the thing that is good, the enemy shall pursue him.

4.text: They have reigned, but not by me: they have been princes, and I knew not: of their silver, and their gold they have made idols to themselves, that they might perish.

5.text: Thy calf, O Samaria, is cast off, my wrath is kindled against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed?

6.text: For itself also is the invention of Israel: a workman made it, and it is no god: for the calf of Samaria shall be turned to spiders’ webs.

7.text: For they shall sow wind, and reap a whirlwind, there is no standing stalk in it, the bud shall yield no meal; and if it should yield, strangers shall eat it.

8.text: Israel is swallowed up: now is he become among the nations like an unclean vessel.

9.text: For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath given gifts to his lovers.

10.text: But even though they shall have hired the nations, now will I gather them together: and they shall rest a while from the burden of the king, and the princes.

11.text: Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin: altars are become to him unto sin.

12.text: I shall write to him my manifold laws, which have been accounted as foreign.

13.text: They shall offer victims, they shall sacrifice flesh, and shall eat it, and the Lord will not receive them: now will he remember their iniquity, and will visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt.

14.text: And Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and hath built temples: and Juda hath built many fenced cities: and I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the houses thereof.

1.text: Rejoice not, O Israel: rejoice not as the nations do: for thou hast committed fornication against thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor.

2.text: The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the wine shall deceive them.

3.text: They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land: Ephraim is returned to Egypt, and hath eaten unclean things among the Assyrians.

4.text: They shall not offer wine to the Lord, neither shall they please him: their sacrifices shall be like the bread of mourners: all that shall eat it shall be defiled: for their bread is life for their soul, it shall not enter into the house of the Lord.

5.text: What will you do in the solemn day, in the day of the feast of the Lord?

6.text: For behold they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them together, Memphis shall bury them: nettles shall inherit their beloved silver, the bur shall be in their tabernacles.

7.text: The days of visitation are come, the days of repaying are come: know ye, O Israel, that the prophet was foolish, the spiritual man was mad, for the multitude of thy iniquity, and the multitude of thy madness.

8.text: The watchman of Ephraim was with my God: the prophet is become a snare of ruin upon all his ways, madness is in the house of his God.

9.text: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa: he will remember their iniquity, and will visit their sin.

10.text: I found Israel like grapes in the desert, I saw their fathers like the firstfruits of the fig tree in the top thereof: but they went in to Beelphegor, and alienated themselves to that confusion, and became abominable, as those things were, which they loved.

11.text: As for Ephraim, their glory hath flown away like a bird from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.

12.text: And though they should bring up their children, I will make them without children among men: yea, and woe to them, when I shall depart from them.

13.text: Ephraim, as I saw, was a Tyre founded in beauty: and Ephraim shall bring out his children to the murderer.

14.text: Give them, O Lord. What wilt thou give them? Give them a womb without children, and dry breasts.

15.text: All their wickedness is in Galgal, for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their devices I will cast them forth out of my house: I will love them no more, all their princes are revolters.

16.text: Ephraim is struck, their root is dried up, they shall yield no fruit. And if they should have issue, I will slay the best beloved fruit of their womb.

17.text: My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

1.text: Israel a vine full of branches, the fruit is agreeable to it: according to the multitude of his fruit he hath multiplied altars, according to the plenty of his land he hath abounded with idols.

2.text: Their heart is divided: now they shall perish: he shall break down their idols, he shall destroy their altars.

3.text: For now they shall say: We have no king: because we fear not the Lord: and what shall a king do to us?

4.text: You speak words of an unprofitable vision, and you shall make a covenant: and judgment shall spring up as bitterness in the furrows of the field.

5.text: The inhabitants of Samaria have worshipped the king of Bethaven: for the people thereof have mourned over it, and the wardens of its temple that rejoiced over it in its glory because it is departed from it.

6.text: For itself also is carried into Assyria, a present to the avenging king: shame shall fall upon Ephraim, and Israel shall be confounded in his own will.

7.text: Samaria hath made her king to pass as froth upon the face of the water.

8.text: And the high places of the idol, the sin of Israel shall be destroyed: the bur and the thistle shall grow up over their altars: and they shall say to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us.

9.text: From the days of Gabaa, Israel hath sinned, there they stood: the battle in Gabaa against the children of iniquity shall not overtake them.

10.text: According to my desire I will chastise them: and the nations shall be gathered together against them, when they shall be chastised for their two iniquities.

11.text: Ephraim is a heifer taught to love to tread out corn, but I passed over upon the beauty of her neck: I will ride upon Ephraim, Juda shall plough, Jacob shall break the furrows for himself.

12.text: Sow for yourselves in justice, and reap in the mouth of mercy, break up your fallow ground: but the time to seek the Lord is, when he shall come that shall teach you justice.

13.text: You have ploughed wickedness, you have reaped iniquity, you have eaten the fruit of lying: because thou hast trusted in thy ways, in the multitude of thy strong ones.

14.text: A tumult shall arise among thy people: and all thy fortresses shall be destroyed as Salmana was destroyed, by the house of him that judged Baal in the day of battle, the mother being dashed in pieces upon her children.

15.text: So hath Bethel done to you, because of the evil of your iniquities.

1.text: As the morning passeth, so hath the king of Israel passed away. Because Israel was a child, and I loved him: and I called my son out of Egypt.

2.text: As they called them, they went away from before their face: they offered victims to Baalim, and sacrificed to idols.

3.text: And I was like a foster father to Ephraim, I carried them in my arms: and they knew not that I healed them.

4.text: I will draw them with the cords of Adam, with the bands of love: and I will be to them as one that taketh off the yoke on their jaws: and I put his meat to him that he might eat.

5.text: He shall not return into the land of Egypt, but the Assyrian shall be his king: because they would not be converted.

6.text: The sword hath begun in his cities, and it shall consume his chosen men, and shall devour their heads.

7.text: And my people shall long for my return: but a yoke shall be put upon them together, which shall not be taken off.

8.text: How shall I deal with thee, O Ephraim, shall I protect thee, O Israel? how shall I make thee as Adama, shall I set thee as Seboim? my heart is turned within me, my repentance is stirred up.

9.text: I will not execute the fierceness of my wrath: I will not return to destroy Ephraim: because I am God, and not man: the holy one in the midst of thee, and I will not enter into the city.

10.text: They shall walk after the Lord, he shall roar as a lion: because he shall roar, and the children of the sea shall fear.

11.text: And they shall fly away like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of the Assyrians: and I will place them in their own houses, saith the Lord.

12.text: Ephraim hath compassed me about with denials, and the house of Israel with deceit: but Juda went down as a witness with God, and is faithful with the saints.

1.text: Ephraim feedeth on the wind, and followeth the burning heat: all the day long he multiplied lies and desolation: and he hath made a covenant with the Assyrians, and carried oil into Egypt.

2.text: Therefore there is a judgment of the Lord with Juda, and a visitation for Jacob: he will render to him according to his ways, and according to his devices.

3.text: In the womb he supplanted his brother: and by his strength he had success with an angel.

4.text: And he prevailed over the angel, and was strengthened: he wept, and made supplication to him: he found him in Bethel, and there he spoke with us.

5.text: Even the Lord the God of hosts, the Lord is his memorial.

6.text: Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and judgment, and hope in thy God always.

7.text: He is like Chanaan, there is a deceitful balance in his hand, he hath loved oppression.

8.text: And Ephraim said: But yet I am become rich, I have found me an idol: all my labours shall not find me the iniquity that I have committed.

9.text: And I that am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, will yet cause thee to dwell in tabernacles, as in the days of the feast.

10.text: And I have spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and I have used similitudes by the ministry of the prophets.

11.text: If Galaad be an idol, then in vain were they in Galgal offering sacrifices with bullocks: for their altars also are as heaps in the furrows of the field.

12.text: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and was a keeper for a wife.

13.text: But the Lord by a prophet brought Israel out of Egypt: and he was preserved by a prophet.

14.text: Ephraim hath provoked me to wrath with his bitterness, and his blood shall come upon him, and his Lord will render his reproach unto him.

1.text: When Ephraim spoke, a horror seized Israel: and he sinned in Baal and died.

2.text: And now they have sinned more and more: and they have made to themselves a molten thing of their silver as the likeness of idols: the whole is the work of craftsmen: to these that say: Sacrifice men, ye that adore calves.

3.text: Therefore they shall be as a morning aloud, and as the early dew that passeth away, as the dust that is driven with a whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.

4.text: But I am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt: and thou shalt know no God but me, and there is no saviour beside me.

5.text: I knew thee in the desert, in the land of the wilderness.

6.text: According to their pastures they were filled, and were made full: and they lifted up their heart, and have forgotten me.

7.text: And I will be to them as a lioness, as a leopard in the way of the Assyrians.

8.text: I will meet them as a bear that is robbed of her whelps, and I will rend the inner parts of their liver: and I will devour them there as a lion, the beast of the field shall tear them.

9.text: Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me.

10.text: Where is thy king? now especially let him save thee in all thy cities: and thy judges, of whom thou saidst: Give me kings and princes.

11.text: I will give thee a king in my wrath, and will take him away in my indignation.

12.text: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up, his sin is hidden.

13.text: The sorrows of a woman in labour snail come upon him, he is an unwise son: for now he shall not stand in the breach of the children.

14.text: I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite: comfort is hidden from my eyes.

15.text: Because he shall make a separation between brothers: the Lord will bring a burning wind that shall rise from the desert, and it shall dry up his springs, and shall make his fountain desolate, and he shall carry off the treasure of every desirable vessel.

16.text: Let Samaria perish, because she hath stirred up her God to bitterness: let them perish by the sword, let their little ones be dashed, and let the women with child be ripped up.

1.text: Return, O Israel, to the Lord thy God: for thou hast fallen down by thy iniquity.

2.text: Take with you words, and return to the Lord, and say to him: Take away all iniquity, and receive the good: and we will render the calves of our lips.

3.text: Assyria shall not save us, we will not ride upon horses, neither will we say any more: The works of our hands are our gods, for thou wilt have mercy on the fatherless that is in thee.

4.text: I will heal their breaches, I will love them freely: for my wrath is turned away from them.

5.text: I will be as the dew, Israel shall spring as the lily, and his root shall shoot forth as that of Libanus.

6.text: His branches shall spread, and his glory shall be as the olive tree: and his smell as that of Libanus.

7.text: They shall be converted that sit under his shadow: they shall live upon wheat, and they shall blossom as a vine: his memorial shall be as the wine of Libanus.

8.text: Ephraim shall say, What have I to do any more with idols? I will hear him, and I will make him flourish like a green fir tree: from me is thy fruit found.

9.text: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know these things? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall in them.

1.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel the son of Phatuel.

2.text: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land: did this ever happen in your days, or in the days of your fathers?

3.text: Tell ye of this to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children to another generation.

4.text: That which the palmerworm hath left, the locust hath eaten: and that which the locust hath left, the bruchus hath eaten: and that which the bruchus hath left, the mildew hath destroyed.

5.text: Awake, ye that are drunk, and weep, and mourn all ye that take delight in drinking sweet wine: for it is cut off from your mouth.

6.text: For a nation is come up upon my land, strong and without number: his teeth are like the teeth of a lion: and his cheek teeth as of a lion’s whelp.

7.text: He hath laid my vineyard waste, and hath pilled off the bark of my fig tree: he hath stripped it bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white.

8.text: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.

9.text: Sacrifice and libation is cut off from the house of the Lord: the priests, the Lord’s ministers, have mourned:

10.text: The country is destroyed, the ground hath mourned: for the corn is wasted, the wine is confounded, the oil hath languished.

11.text: The husbandmen are ashamed, the vinedressers have howled for the wheat, and for the barley, because the harvest of the field is perished.

12.text: The vineyard is confounded, and the fig tree hath languished: the pomegranate tree, and the palm tree, and the apple tree, and all the trees of the field are withered: because joy is withdrawn from the children of men.

13.text: Gird yourselves, and lament, O ye priests, howl, ye ministers of the altars: go in, lie in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: because sacrifice and libation is cut off from the house of your God.

14.text: Sanctify ye a fast, call an assembly; gather together the ancients, all the inhabitants of the land into the house of your God: and cry ye to the Lord:

15.text: Ah, ah, ah, for the day: because the day of the Lord is at hand, and it shall come like destruction from the mighty.

16.text: Is not your food cut off before your eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?

17.text: The beasts have rotted in their dung, the barns are destroyed, the storehouses are broken down: because the corn is confounded.

18.text: Why did the beast groan, why did the herds of cattle low? because there is no pasture for them: yea, and the flocks of sheep are perished.

19.text: To thee, O Lord, will I cry: because fire hath devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness, and the flame hath burnt all the trees of the country.

20.text: Yea and the beasts of the field have looked up to thee, as a garden bed that thirsteth after rain, for the springs of waters are dried up, and fire hath devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.

1.text: Blow ye the trumpet in Sion, sound an alarm in my holy mountain, let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: because the day of the Lord cometh, because it is nigh at hand,

2.text: A day of darkness, and of gloominess, a day of clouds and whirlwinds: a numerous and strong people as the morning spread upon the mountains: the like to it hath not been from the beginning, nor shall be after it even to the years of generation and generation.

3.text: Before the face thereof a devouring fire, and behind it a burning flame: the land is like a garden of pleasure before it, and behind it a desolate wilderness, neither is there any one that can escape it.

4.text: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses, and they shall run like horsemen.

5.text: They shall leap like the noise of chariots upon the tops of mountains, like the noise of a flame of fire devouring the stubble, as a strong people prepared to battle.

6.text: At their presence the people shall be in grievous pains: all faces shall be made like a kettle.

7.text: They shall run like valiant men: like men of war they shall scale the wall: the men shall march every one on his way, and they shall not turn aside from their ranks.

8.text: No one shall press upon his brother: they shall walk every one in his path: yea, and they shall fall through the windows, and shall take no harm.

9.text: They shall enter into the city: they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up the houses, they shall come in at the windows as a thief.

10.text: At their presence the earth hath trembled, the heavens are moved: the sun and moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining.

11.text: And the Lord hath uttered his voice before the face of his army: for his armies are exceedingly great, for they are strong and execute his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible: and who can stand it?

12.text: Now therefore saith the Lord: Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning.

13.text: And rend your hearts, and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy, and ready to repent of the evil.

14.text: Who knoweth but he will return, and forgive, and leave a blessing behind him, sacrifice and libation to the Lord your God?

15.text: Blow the trumpet in Sion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly,

16.text: Gather together the people, sanctify the church, assemble the ancients, gather together the little ones, and them that suck at the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bride chamber.

17.text: Between the porch and the altar the priests the Lord’s ministers shall weep, and shall say: Spare, O Lord, spare thy people: and give not thy inheritance to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them. Why should they say among the nations: Where is their God?

18.text: The Lord hath been zealous for his land, and hath spared his people.

19.text: And the Lord answered and said to his people: Behold I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and you shall be filled with them: and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations.

20.text: And I will remove far off from you the northern enemy: and I will drive him into a land unpassable, and desert, with his face towards the east sea, and his hinder part towards the utmost sea: and his stench shall ascend, and his rottenness shall go up, because he hath done proudly.

21.text: Fear not, O land, be glad and rejoice: for the Lord hath done great things.

22.text: Fear not, ye beasts of the fields: for the beautiful places of the wilderness are sprung, for the tree hath brought forth its fruit, the fig tree, and the vine have yielded their strength.

23.text: And you, O children of Sion, rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God: because he hath given you a teacher of justice, and he will make the early and the latter rain to come down to you as in the beginning.

24.text: And the floors shall be filled with wheat, and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil.

25.text: And I will restore to you the ears which the locust, and the bruchus, and the mildew, and the palmerworm have eaten; my great host which I sent upon you.

26.text: And you shall eat in plenty, and shall be filled: and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God, who hath done wonders with you, and my people shall not be confounded for ever.

27.text: And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel: and I am the Lord your God, and there is none besides: and my people shall not be confounded for ever.

28.text: And it shall come to pass after this, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy: your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.

29.text: Moreover upon my servants and handmaids in those days I will pour forth my spirit.

30.text: And I will shew wonders in heaven; and in earth, blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke.

31.text: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood: before the great and dreadful day of the Lord doth come.

32.text: And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved: for in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem shall be salvation, as the Lord hath said, and in the residue whom the Lord shall call.

1.text: For behold in those days, and in that time when I shall bring back the captivity of Juda and Jerusalem:

2.text: I will gather together all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Josaphat: and I will plead with them there for my people, and for my inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and have parted my land.

3.text: And they have cast lots upon my people: and the boy they have put in the stews, and the girl they have sold for wine, that they might drink.

4.text: But what have you to do with me, O Tyre, and Sidon, and all the coast of the Philistines? will you revenge yourselves on me? and if you revenge yourselves on me, I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head.

5.text: For you have taken away my silver and my gold: and my desirable and most beautiful things you have carried into your temples.

6.text: And the children of Juda, and the children of Jerusalem you have sold to the children of the Greeks, that you might remove them far off from their own country.

7.text: Behold, I will raise them up out of the place wherein you have sold them: and I will return your recompense upon your own heads.

8.text: And I will sell your sons, and your daughters by the hands of the children of Juda, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, a nation far off, for the Lord hath spoken it.

9.text: Proclaim ye this among the nations: prepare war, rouse up the strong: let them come, let all the men of war come up.

10.text: Cut your ploughshares into swords, and your spades into spears. Let the weak say: I am strong.

11.text: Break forth, and come, all ye nations, from round about, and gather yourselves together: there will the Lord cause all thy strong ones to fall down.

12.text: Let them arise, and let the nations come up into the valley of Josaphat: for there I will sit to judge all nations round about.

13.text: Put ye in the sickles, for the harvest is ripe: come and go down, for the press is full, the fats run over: for their wickedness is multiplied.

14.text: Nations, nations in the valley of destruction: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of destruction.

15.text: The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining.

16.text: And the Lord shall roar out of Sion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem: and the heavens and the earth shall be moved, and the Lord shall be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.

17.text: And you shall know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Sion my holy mountain: and Jerusalem shall be holy and strangers shall pass through it no more.

18.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk: and waters shall flow through all the rivers of Juda: and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord, and shall water the torrent of thorns.

19.text: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom a wilderness destroyed: because they have done unjustly against the children of Juda, and have shed innocent blood in their land.

20.text: And Judea shall be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generation and generation.

21.text: And I will cleanse their blood which I had not cleansed: and the Lord will dwell in Sion.

1.text: The words of Amos, who was among herdsmen of Thecua: which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Ozias king of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel two years before the earthquake.

2.text: And he said: The Lord will roar from Sion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem: and the beautiful places of the shepherds have mourned, and the top of Carmel is withered.

3.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Damascus, and for four I will not convert it: because they have thrashed Galaad with iron wains.

4.text: And I will send a fire into the house of Azael, and it shall devour the houses of Benadad.

5.text: And I will break the bar of Damascus: and I will cut off the inhabitants from the plain of the idol, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of pleasure: and the people of Syria shall be carried away to Cyrene, saith the Lord.

6.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Gaza, and for four I will not convert it: because they have carried away a perfect captivity to shut them up in Edom.

7.text: And I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it shall devour the houses thereof.

8.text: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Azotus, and him that holdeth the sceptre from Ascalon: and I will turn my hand against Accaron, and the rest of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord God.

9.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four I will not convert it: because they have shut up an entire captivity in Edom, and have not remembered the covenant of brethren.

10.text: And I will send a fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it shall devour the houses thereof.

11.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Edom, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath pursued his brother with the sword, and hath cast off all pity, and hath carried on his fury, and hath kept his wrath to the end.

12.text: I will send a fire into Theman: and it shall devour the houses of Bosra.

13.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of the children of Ammon, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath ripped up the women with child of Galaad to enlarge his border.

14.text: And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabba: and it shall devour the houses thereof with shouting in the day of battle, and with a whirlwind in the day of trouble.

15.text: And Melchom shall go into captivity, both he, and his princes together, saith the Lord.

1.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Moab, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath burnt the bones of the king of Edom even to ashes.

2.text: And I will send a fire into Moab, and it shall devour the houses of Carioth: and Moab shall die with a noise, with the sound of the trumpet:

3.text: And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all his princes with him, saith the Lord.

4.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Juda, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath cast away the law of the Lord, and hath not kept his commandments: for their idols have caused them to err, after which their fathers have walked.

5.text: And I will send a fire into Juda, and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem.

6.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath sold the just man for silver, and the poor man for a pair of shoes.

7.text: They bruise the heads of the poor upon the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the humble: and the son and his father have gone to the same young woman, to profane my holy name.

8.text: And they sat down upon garments laid to pledge by every altar: and drank the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.

9.text: Yet I cast out the Amorrhite before their face: whose height was like the height of cedars, and who was strong as an oak: and I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots beneath.

10.text: It is I that brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and I led you forty years through the wilderness, that you might possess the land of the Amorrhite.

11.text: And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not so, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord?

12.text: And you will present wine to the Nazarites: and command the prophets, saying: Prophesy not.

13.text: Behold, I will screak under you as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay.

14.text: And flight shall perish from the swift, and the valiant shall not possess his strength, neither shall the strong save his life.

15.text: And he that holdeth the bow shall not stand, and the swift of foot shall not escape, neither shall the rider of the horse save his life.

16.text: And the stout of heart among the valiant shall flee away naked in that day, saith the Lord.

1.text: Hear the word that the Lord hath spoken concerning you, O ye children of Israel: concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:

2.text: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore will I visit upon you all your iniquities.

3.text: Shall two walk together except they be agreed?

4.text: Will a lion roar in the forest, if he have no prey? will the lion’s whelp cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?

5.text: Will the bird fall into the snare upon the earth, if there be no fowler? Shall the snare be taken up from the earth, before it hath taken somewhat?

6.text: Shall the trumpet sound in a city, and the people not be afraid? Shall there be evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done?

7.text: For the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets.

8.text: The lion shall roar, who will not fear? The Lord God hath spoken, who shall not prophesy?

9.text: Publish it in the houses of Azotus, and in the houses of the land of Egypt, and say: Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the many follies in the midst thereof, and them that suffer oppression in the inner rooms thereof.

10.text: And they have not known to do the right thing, saith the Lord, storing up iniquity, and robberies in their houses.

11.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: The land shall be in tribulation, and shall be compassed about: and thy strength shall be taken away from thee, and thy houses shall be spoiled.

12.text: Thus saith the Lord: As if a shepherd should get out of the lion’s mouth two legs, or the tip of the ear: so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria, in a piece of a bed, and in the couch of Damascus.

13.text: Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord the God of hosts:

14.text: That in the day when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel, I will visit upon him, and upon the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altars shall be cut off, and shall fall to the ground.

15.text: And I will strike the winter house with the summer house: and the houses of ivory shall perish, and many houses shall be destroyed, saith the Lord.

1.text: Hear this word, ye fat kine that are in the mountains of Samaria: you that oppress the needy, and crush the poor: that say to your masters: Bring, and we will drink.

2.text: The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness, that lo, the days shall come upon you, when they shall lift you up on pikes, and what shall remain of you in boiling pots.

3.text: And you shall go out at the breaches one over against the other, and you shall be cast forth into Armon, saith the Lord.

4.text: Come ye to Bethel, and do wickedly: to Galgal, and multiply transgressions: and bring in the morning your victims, your tithes in three days.

5.text: And offer a sacrifice of praise with leaven: and call free offerings, and proclaim it: for so you would do, O children of Israel, saith the Lord God.

6.text: Whereupon I also have given you dulness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet you have not returned to me, saith the Lord.

7.text: I also have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon: and the piece whereupon I rained not, withered.

8.text: And two and three cities went to one city to drink water, and were not filled: yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord.

9.text: I struck you with a burning wind, and with mildew, the palmerworm hath eaten up your many gardens, and your vineyards: your olive groves, and fig groves: yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord.

10.text: I sent death upon you in the way of Egypt, I slew your young men with the sword, even to the captivity of your horses: and I made the stench of your camp to come up into your nostrils: yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord.

11.text: I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha, and you were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning: yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord.

12.text: Therefore I will do these things to thee, O Israel: and after I shall have done these things to thee, be prepared to meet thy God, O Israel.

13.text: For behold he that formeth the mountains and createth the wind, and declareth his word to man, he that maketh the morning mist, and walketh upon the high places of the earth: the Lord the God of hosts is his name.

1.text: Hear ye this word, which I take up concerning you for a lamentation. The house of Israel is fallen, and it shall rise no more.

2.text: The virgin of Israel is cast down upon her land, there is none to raise her up.

3.text: For thus saith the Lord God: The city, out of which came forth a thousand, there shall be left in it a hundred: and out of which there came a hundred, there shall be left in it ten, in the house of Israel.

4.text: For thus saith the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek ye me, and you shall live.

5.text: But seek not Bethel, and go not into Galgal, neither shall you pass over to Bersabee: for Galgal shall go into captivity, and Bethel shall be unprofitable.

6.text: Seek ye the Lord, and live: lest the house of Joseph be burnt with fire, and it shall devour, and there shall be none to quench Bethel.

7.text: You that turn judgment into wormwood, and forsake justice in the land,

8.text: Seek him that maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and that turneth darkness into morning, and that changeth day into night: that calleth the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.

9.text: He that with a smile bringeth destruction upon the strong, and waste upon the mighty.

10.text: They have hated him that rebuketh in the gate: and have abhorred him that speaketh perfectly.

11.text: Therefore because you robbed the poor, and took the choice prey from him: you shall build houses with square stone, and shall not dwell in them: you shall plant most delightful vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them.

12.text: Because I know your manifold crimes, and your grievous sins: enemies of the just, taking bribes, and oppressing the poor in the gate.

13.text: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence at that time, for it is an evil time.

14.text: Seek ye good, and not evil, that you may live: and the Lord the God of hosts will be with you, as you have said.

15.text: Hate evil, and love good, and establish judgment in the gate: it may be the Lord the God of hosts may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.

16.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord the God of hosts the sovereign Lord: In every street there shall be wailing: and in all places that are without, they shall say: Alas, alas! and they shall call the husbandman to mourning, and such as are skillful in lamentation to lament.

17.text: And in all vineyards there shall be wailing: because I will pass through in the midst of thee, saith the Lord.

18.text: Woe to them that desire the day of the Lord: to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.

19.text: As if a man should flee from the face of a lion, and a bear should meet him: or enter into the house, and lean with his hand upon the wall, and a serpent should bite him.

20.text: Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness, and not light: and obscurity, and no brightness in it?

21.text: I hate, and have rejected your festivities: and I will not receive the odour of your assemblies.

22.text: And if you offer me holocausts, and your gifts, I will not receive them: neither will I regard the vows of your fat beasts.

23.text: Take away from me the tumult of thy songs: and I will not hear the canticles of thy harp.

24.text: But judgment shall be revealed as water, and justice as a mighty torrent.

25.text: Did you offer victims and sacrifices to me in the desert for forty years, O house of Israel?

26.text: But you carried a tabernacle for your Moloch, and the image of your idols, the star of your god, which you made to yourselves.

27.text: And I will cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, the God of hosts is his name.

1.text: Woe to you that are wealthy in Sion, and to you that have confidence in the mountain of Samaria: ye great men, heads of the people, that go in with state into the house of Israel.

2.text: Pass ye over to Chalane, and see, and go from thence into Emath the great: and go down into Geth of the Philistines, and to all the best kingdoms of these: if their border be larger than your border.

3.text: You that are separated unto the evil day: and that approach to the throne of iniquity;

4.text: You that sleep upon beds of ivory, and are wanton on your couches: that eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the herd;

5.text: You that sing to the sound of the psaltery: they have thought themselves to have instruments of music like David;

6.text: That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best ointments: and they are not concerned for the affliction of Joseph.

7.text: Wherefore now they shall go captive at the head of them that go into captivity: and the faction of the luxurious ones shall be taken away.

8.text: The Lord God hath sworn by his own soul, saith the Lord the God of hosts: I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his houses, and I will deliver up the city with the inhabitants thereof.

9.text: And if there remain ten men in one house, they also shall die.

10.text: And a man’s kinsman shall take him up, and shall burn him, that he may carry the bones out of the house; and he shall say to him that is in the inner rooms of the house: Is there yet any with thee? And he shall answer: There is an end. And he shall any to him: Hold thy peace, and mention not the name of the Lord.

11.text: For behold the Lord hath commanded, and he will strike the greater house with breaches, and the lesser house with clefts.

12.text: Can horses run upon the rocks, or can any one plough with buffles? for you have turned judgment into bitterness, and the fruit of justice into wormwood.

13.text: You that rejoice in a thing of nought: you that say: Have we not taken unto us horns by our own strength?

14.text: But behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel, saith the Lord the God of hosts; and they shall destroy you from the entrance of Emath, even to the torrent of the desert.

1.text: These things the Lord God shewed to me: and behold the locust was formed in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter rain, and lo, it was the latter rain after the king’s mowing.

2.text: And it came to pass, that when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land, I said: O Lord God, be merciful, I beseech thee: who shall raise up Jacob, for he is very little?

3.text: The Lord had pity upon this: It shall not be, said the Lord.

4.text: These things the Lord God shewed to me: and behold the Lord called for judgment unto fire, and it devoured the great deep, and ate up a part at the same time.

5.text: And I said: O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee, who shall raise up Jacob, for he is a little one?

6.text: The Lord had pity upon this. Yea this also shall not be, said the Lord God.

7.text: These things the Lord shewed to me: and behold the Lord was standing upon a plastered wall, and in his hand a mason’s trowel.

8.text: And the Lord said to me: What seest thou, Amos? And I said: A mason’s trowel. And the Lord said: Behold, I will lay down the trowel in the midst of my people Israel. I will plaster them over no more.

9.text: And the high places of the idol shall be thrown down, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste: and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

10.text: And Amasias the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos hath rebelled against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.

11.text: For thus saith Amos: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be carried away captive out of their own land.

12.text: And Amasias said to Amos: Thou seer, go, flee away into the land of Juda: and eat bread there, and prophesy there.

13.text: But prophesy not again any more in Bethel: because it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is the house of the kingdom.

14.text: And Amos answered and said to Amasias: I am not a prophet, nor am I the son of a prophet: but I am a herdsman plucking wild figs.

15.text: And the Lord took me when I followed the flock, and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel.

16.text: And now hear thou the word of the Lord: Thou sayest, thou shalt not prophesy against Israel, and thou shalt not drop thy word upon the house of the idol.

17.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord: Thy wife shall play the harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be measured by a line: and thou shalt die in a polluted land, and Israel shall go into captivity out of their land.

1.text: These things the Lord shewed to me: and behold a hook to draw down the fruit.

2.text: And he said: What seest thou, Amos? And I said: A hook to draw down fruit. And the Lord said to me: The end is come upon my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more.

3.text: And the hinges of the temple shall screak in that day, saith the Lord God: many shall die: silence shall be cast in every place.

4.text: Hear this, you that crush the poor, and make the needy of the land to fail,

5.text: Saying: When will the month be over, and we shall sell our wares: and the sabbath, and we shall open the corn: that we may lessen the measure, and increase the sicle, and may convey in deceitful balances,

6.text: That we may possess the needy for money, and the poor for a pair of shoes, and may sell the refuse of the corn?

7.text: The Lord hath sworn against the pride of Jacob: surely I will never forget all their works.

8.text: Shall not the land tremble for this, and every one mourn that dwelleth therein: and rise up altogether as a river, and be cast out, and run down as the river of Egypt?

9.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord God, that the sun shall go down at midday, and I will make the earth dark in the day of light:

10.text: And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation: and I will bring up sackcloth upon every back of yours, and baldness upon every head: and I will make it as the mourning of an only son, and the latter end thereof as a bitter day.

11.text: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will send forth a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord.

12.text: And they shall move from sea to sea, and from the north to the east: they shall go about seeking the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.

13.text: In that day the fair virgins, and the young men shall faint for thirst.

14.text: They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say: Thy God, O Dan, liveth: and the way of Bersabee liveth: and they shall fall, and shall rise no more.

1.text: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he said: Strike the hinges, and let the lintels be shook: for there is covetousness in the head of them all, and I will slay the last of them with the sword: there shall be no flight for them: they shall flee, and he that shall flee of them shall not be delivered.

2.text: Though they go down even to hell, thence shall my hand bring them out: and though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down.

3.text: And though they be hid in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them away from thence: and though they hide themselves from my eyes in the depth of the sea, there will I command the serpent and he shall bite them.

4.text: And if they go into captivity before their enemies, there will I command the sword, and it shall kill them. And I will set my eyes upon them for evil, and not for good.

5.text: And the Lord the God of hosts is he who toucheth the earth, and it shall melt: and all that dwell therein shall mourn: and it shall rise up as a river, and shall run down as the river of Egypt.

6.text: He that buildeth his ascension in heaven, and hath founded his bundle upon the earth: who calleth the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth, the Lord is his name.

7.text: Are not you as the children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel, saith the Lord? did not I bring up Israel, out of the land of Egypt: and the Philistines out of Cappadocia, and the Syrians out of Cyrene?

8.text: Behold the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth: but yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.

9.text: For behold I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, as corn is sifted in a sieve: and there shall not a little stone fall to the ground.

10.text: All the sinners of my people shall fall by the sword: who say: The evils shall not approach, and shall not come upon us.

11.text: In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David, that is fallen: and I will close up the breaches of the walls thereof, and repair what was fallen: and I will rebuild it as in the days of old.

12.text: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all nations, because my name is invoked upon them: saith the Lord that doth these things.

13.text: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, when the ploughman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed: and the mountains shall drop sweetness, and every hill shall be tilled.

14.text: And I will bring back the captivity of my people Israel: and they shall build the abandoned cities, and inhabit them: and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine of them: and shall make gardens, and eat the fruits of them.

15.text: And I will plant them upon their own land: and I will no more pluck them out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.

1.text: The vision of Abdias. Thus saith the Lord God to Edom: We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and he hath sent an ambassador to the nations: Arise, and let us rise up to battle against him.

2.text: Behold I have made thee small among the nations: thou art exceeding contemptible.

3.text: The pride of thy heart hath lifted thee up, who dwellest in the clefts of the rocks, and settest up thy throne on high: who sayest in thy heart: Who shall bring me down to the ground?

4.text: Though thou be exalted as an eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars: thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.

5.text: If thieves had gone in to thee, if robbers by night, how wouldst thou have held thy peace? would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers had come in to thee, would they not have left thee at the least a cluster?

6.text: How have they searched Esau, how have they sought out his hidden things?

7.text: They have sent thee out even to the border: all the men of thy confederacy have deceived thee: the men of thy peace have prevailed against thee: they that eat with thee shall lay snares under thee: there is no wisdom in him.

8.text: Shall not I in that day, saith the Lord, destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?

9.text: And thy valiant men of the south shall be afraid, that man may be cut off from the mount of Esau.

10.text: For the slaughter, and for the iniquity against thy brother Jacob, confusion shall cover thee, and thou shalt perish for ever.

11.text: In the day when thou stoodest against him, when strangers carried away his army captive, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem: thou also wast as one of them.

12.text: But thou shalt not look on in the day of thy brother, in the day of his leaving his country: and thou shalt not rejoice over the children of Juda, in the day of their destruction: and thou shalt not magnify thy mouth in the day of distress.

13.text: Neither shalt thou enter into the gate of my people in the day of their ruin: neither shalt thou also look on in his evils in the day of his calamity: and thou shalt not be sent out against his army in the day of his desolation.

14.text: Neither shalt thou stand in the crossways to kill them that flee: and thou shalt not shut up them that remain of him in the day of tribulation.

15.text: For the day of the Lord is at hand upon all nations: as thou hast done, so shall it be done to thee: he will turn thy reward upon thy own head.

16.text: For as you have drunk upon my holy mountain, so all nations shall drink continually: and they shall drink, and sup up, and they shall be as though they were not.

17.text: And in mount Sion shall be salvation, and it shall be holy, and the house of Jacob shall possess those that possessed them.

18.text: And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble: and they shall be kindled in them, and shall devour them: and there shall be no remains of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it.

19.text: And they that are toward the south, shall inherit the mount of Esau, and they that are in the plains, the Philistines: and they shall possess the country of Ephraim, and the country of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Galaad.

20.text: And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel, all the places of the Chanaanites even to Sarepta: and the captivity of Jerusalem that is in Bosphorus, shall possess the cities of the south.

21.text: And saviours shall come up into mount Sion to judge the mount of Esau: and the kingdom shall be for the Lord.

1.text: Now the word of the Lord came to Jonas the son of Amathi, saying:

2.text: Arise, and go to Ninive the great city, and preach in it: for the wickedness thereof is come up before me.

3.text: And Jonas rose up to flee into Tharsis from the face of the Lord, and he went down to Joppe, and found a ship going to Tharsis: and he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them to Tharsis from the face of the Lord.

4.text: But the Lord sent a great wind into the sea: and a great tempest was raised in the sea, and the ship was in danger to be broken.

5.text: And the mariners were afraid, and the men cried to their god: and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship, into the sea, to lighten it of them: and Jonas went down into the inner part of the ship, and fell into a deep sleep.

6.text: And the shipmaster came to him, and said to him: Why art thou fast asleep? rise up, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think of us, that we may not perish.

7.text: And they said every one to his fellow: Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know why this evil is upon us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonas.
